question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer, CIO of Lotus Cat III AIF, is briefing his IC on how 'market efficiency' should be interpreted when framing the fund's alpha thesis. Which of the following best distinguishes 'Informational Efficiency' from 'Operational Efficiency' in capital markets?

answer.text: Informational efficiency relates to how quickly and fully prices reflect available information, whereas operational efficiency concerns the cost of transacting (impact cost, brokerage, bid-ask).
Informational efficiency measures settlement cycle time, whereas operational efficiency measures the speed of news dissemination.
Informational efficiency refers to the average spread in the order book, whereas operational efficiency refers to the accuracy of analyst forecasts.
Both terms are interchangeable and simply mean that the market is liquid and well-regulated.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 3.1, operational efficiency is about the cost of carrying out trades (transaction / impact cost); informational efficiency is about prices 'fully reflecting' up-to-date information so that market price becomes an unbiased estimate of fair value. The two are distinct concepts and market-efficiency literature usually refers to informational efficiency. The Trap: Option B conflates settlement operations with informational content. Option C inverts the definitions. Option D treats them as synonyms - a common confusion among junior AIFM analysts.
